mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up this journey through "Girl, Interrupted," I hope you’re feeling a little more seen, a little more understood. Healing—well, it’s not some finish line you cross once and for all. It’s a collection of moments, big and small. Sometimes you’ll feel brave, other times it’s all you can do to just keep going. And honestly, that’s okay. The road through mental illness, through hospital walls and back into everyday life, rarely moves in a straight line. There’ll be setbacks, tiny wins, and a whole lot of learning to live with not knowing what comes next. So here’s what I hope you’ll remember: Healing isn’t a place you arrive and then leave behind. It’s an ongoing process. Labels—sure, they can offer clarity, but they’ll never capture everything that makes you, you. Real connection, the honest kind, can anchor you when things feel out of control. And when you stumble? That doesn’t mean you’ve failed. It’s just another part of finding your way back to wholeness. Most importantly, your story is yours. And sharing it might just light the way for someone else. If you’re struggling right now, please know you’re not alone. Life can be overwhelming, and carrying all those expectations—yours and everyone else’s—gets heavy. But there’s real strength in showing your vulnerability, and so much courage in reaching out for help. The true lessons from "Girl, Interrupted" aren’t only about surviving institutional walls. They’re about embracing the messiness, the beauty, and the uncertainty of being human. You have every right to take up space, to ask for what you need, and to move at your own pace. Healing probably won’t look the way you pictured it. But it’s possible, and it’s yours to define. Just keep moving forward. The story isn’t over yet—and neither is yours.
